title: Tailguard controller synthesis lablog
content:
Purpose and quick thesis:
This is a living lab log for the "Tailguard" controller prototype — a runtime-side admission/flush controller that adaptively enforces per-quantile latency guardrails while preserving batching efficiency and multi-tenant fairness. The goal: reduce 99.9/99.99 tail spikes without regressing p50 and throughput more than 5%.

High-level idea (sketch):
- Maintain lightweight online estimates of per-tenant/request-class quantiles (p50/p95/p99/p999) using reservoir summaries and exponential decay.
- If an incoming request would cause the current batch to likely push any observed quantile over its guardrail, the controller either: 1) flushes the batch early (favoring short requests), 2) delays the request briefly (for affinity), or 3) demotes to a fast-path single-request slot (preemptive isolation).
- Use a circuit-breaker-style hysteresis to avoid oscillation under bursty arrivals. Tuning knobs: quantile window, hysteresis thresholds, demotion budget per-slot, preemption cost model.

Why different from previous batch heuristics:
- Prior work focused on static timeouts and age-weighting; Tailguard couples live quantile estimates to admission decisions and explicitly reasons about fairness budgets so a noisy tenant can't starve others.
- We target extreme tails (p999) and want a predictable, bounded worst-case even in microburst regimes.

Experiment harness (how we measure):
- Runner: local cluster replay harness (replayctl) built from production microtrace captures (sampled by tenant id).
- Workloads: three mixes: steady web (many short), enterprise (mixed lengths), conversational (long streaming). Each run 30m steady-state after warmup.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (per-tenant and global), average batch size, tokens/sec, kernel (compute) time per-batch, blocking time (queue wait), eviction/prefill interactions, fairness score (Jain-like on latency SLO violations).
- Commands (replay):
  ./replayctl --trace=enterprise-sampled.pb --duration=1800 --config=tailguard/experiment-A.yaml --out=run-A
  ./replayctl --compare run-A run-baseline

Controller variants tested:
- baseline: current age-weighted timeouts + urgency weights (no guardrails)
- TG-basic: Tailguard with p99 guardrail, demotion budget 2 slots/second, hysteresis 20%
- TG-tight: p99->p95 gradient enforcement, demotion budget 5 slots/sec, hysteresis 10%
- TG-soft: p999-only enforcement, conservative demotion budget, long hysteresis

Key configuration snippet (experiment-A.yaml):
- quantile_window_secs: 30
- quantile_decay_alpha: 0.15
- guardrails: {p95_ms: 50, p99_ms: 120, p999_ms: 600}
- demotion_budget_per_core_per_sec: 3
- hysteresis_fraction: 0.2
- single_slot_preemption_cost_ms: 6

Profiling approach:
- End-to-end traces with microtrace annotation (request enqueue, batch formation, kernel start/stop, kv-cache lookup, send)
- Perf hotspots: sampled stacks while running replay with TG-tight (perf + flamegraph)
- Instrumented cost accounting: per-request wait vs compute vs demotion overhead

Selected observations (TG-tight vs baseline, enterprise trace):
- Global p999 improved from 840ms -> 310ms (63% reduction).
- p50 regressed +4% (from 28ms -> 29ms), within target.
- Average batch size down 9% (11.5 -> 10.5), tokens/sec -6% on heavy-long workload.
- Fairness score improved: tenants that previously saw recurring p999 spikes dropped violation rate by ~72% while noisy tenant got demoted occasionally (demotion events logged).
- Microtrace insight: many p999 spikes were caused by 1) a long request joining an in-flight batch of short requests and 2) cache thrash due to interleaving of long LLM sessions with short classification queries. Tailguard successfully either demoted the long request or flushed earlier.
- Kernel hotspots: demotion path adds ~5% CPU overhead in admission path (small) but removes expensive kernel stalls caused by large KV cache warmups.

Failure modes and caveats:
- Oscillation in synthetic sawtooth bursts when hysteresis too small -> leads to excessive flushes, hurting throughput. Observed at hysteresis_fraction <= 0.05.
- Overly aggressive demotion budget causes p50 regressions beyond 10% in short-heavy workloads.
- Under high multi-tenant load, per-tenant quantile estimates can be noisy; we need minimum sample thresholds to avoid overreacting to single events.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Can we replace reservoir quantiles with lightweight eCDF sketches to reduce memory and increase responsiveness? Hypothesis: sketches reduce tail noise and stabilize hysteresis decisions.
- Interaction with KV cache length: demoting a long request to a single-slot often avoids cache thrash, but increases downstream kernel inefficiency for that tenant. Measure net tokens/sec per-tenant.
- Can scheduling hint metadata from clients (estimated output tokens) improve decisions? Risk: adversarial clients misreporting. Need signed hints in dedicated deployments.

Next-run plan (short-term):
- Run TG-tight with sketch-based quantiles (proto impl) on conversational trace; measure p999 and tokens/sec. (Ethan)
- Add minimum-sample safeguard (n>=8) before enforcing guardrails per-tenant per-window. (Leila)
- Add telemetry: counter for hysteresis-triggered flushes, demotions, and single-slot preemptions with tenant ids. Expose as per-core metrics. (Ravi)

Notes-to-self (misc):
- Check JIRA-RT-3421 for discussion thread on demotion budget sizing and SLO language.
- Benchmark: use kernel-instrumented replay to see if demoted single-slot path becomes new hotspot at scale; if so, offload admission logic to faster code-path (C++ hot path) and keep control plane decisions in Go.
- Remember to run burst-sawtooth stress with 1s period to validate hysteresis floor.

Raw sample logs (excerpt):
[2024-11-20T15:12:04Z] admission: tenant=acme, len_est=480, batch_len=9, est_p99_after=410, guardrail_p99=300 -> DECISION=DEMOTE slot=core-3 reason=protect-p99
[2024-11-20T15:12:04Z] trace: microtrace_id=xyz kernel_ms=78 queue_ms=19 total_ms=104 (demoted path)

Acceptance criteria for pilot rollout:
- global p999 reduction >= 50% across mixed traces vs baseline
- p50 regression <= 7% on short-heavy runs
- throughput loss <= 8% tokens/sec on conversational runs
- telemetry shows demotion events are < 5% of requests on normal traffic

If pilot passes, roadmap items:
- integrate with rollout API: per-customer guardrail overrides + per-route profiles
- add offline autotune to recommend hysteresis and demotion budgets based on historical traces
- add secure client hints for dedicated/private deployments

References and links:
- design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinc/RT/Tailguard-Design
- GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- replay traces used: enterprise-sampled.pb, convo-long-sampled.pb

End of lablog (working document) - latest: 2024-12-03.
